correctness.rationale: Baychkov et al. Definition 6 directly yields primary coverage and secondary coverage-plus-double-approvals for two seats. All three-candidate strong-nonnesting profiles have a unique best singleton A and pair BC. Exact support inequalities and lexicographic tie cases prove v,w≥u+1 and p,q≥r+2, hence n≥6+3u+3r+t+e. Equality forces the unique six-voter ballot multiset; its singleton support scores are (4,3,3) and BC covers 6 rather than 5. Standalone verifier independently exhausts 3002 anonymous profiles with zero failures at n≤5 and exactly 3 relabeled failures at n=6. The finite check does not replace the infinite inequality argument.

value.rationale: Adams-AV is a newly characterized upper-quota-supporting extension of Adams apportionment. A natural structural consistency question is whether adding a committee seat can eject an unambiguously elected candidate. The result gives the exact smallest tie-breaking-independent witness, a complete equality classification, and strict inequalities explaining why secondary-stage refinements cannot create smaller failures. It supplies a rigorous interpretable counterexample for comparing quota satisfaction with committee-size consistency; the scope is narrow but the cut-off is intrinsic rather than an arbitrary enumeration slice.
